paper.title: Budget-Constrained Multi-Armed Bandits with Multiple Plays

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic budget-constrained MAB with multiple plays
unmapped: each arm also has i.i.d. random costs with support [c_min, 1], c_min > 0; the game stops when the round's cost exceeds the remaining budget B
regret compared against playing the K arms with the largest bang-per-buck ratios mu_r/mu_c
the learner knows c_min (used in the UCB exploration term)
settings.definition_quote: each arm indexed by $i\in [N]$ is associated with an unknown reward and cost distribution with unknown means $0 < \mu_r^i \leq 1$ and $0 < c_{\min} \leq \mu_c^i \leq 1$, respectively. Realizations of costs $c_{i,t} \in [c_{\min}, 1]$ and rewards $r_{i,t} \in [0,1]$ are independently and identically distributed. At each round $t$, the decision maker plays exactly $K$ arms ($1 \leq K \leq N$) and subsequently observes the individual costs and rewards only for the played arms

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial budget-constrained MAB with multiple plays
unmapped: adversarial costs c_i(t) in (c_min, 1) observed for played arms; game ends when a round's cost exceeds remaining budget B
for Theorem 2 the learner knows an upper bound g on G_max
settings.definition_quote: For each arm $i$ played at round $t$, the player observes the reward $r_i(t)\in [0, 1]$ and, unlike in previous settings, additionally the cost $0 < c_{\min} < c_i(t) < 1$. As in the stochastic setting, the player is given a budget $B > 0$ to pay for the costs incurred, and the algorithm terminates after $\tau_{\mathcal{A}}(B)$ rounds when the sum of materialized costs in round $\tau_{\mathcal{A}}(B)$ exceeds the remaining budget.

symbols.c_min: lower bound on the support of the cost distributions

source.label: thm:stochastic_case_sublinear_regret
source.quote: There exist constants $c_1$, $c_2$, and $c_3$, which are functions of $N, K, c_{\min}, \Delta_{\min}, \mu_{i}, \mu_c$ only, such that Algorithm \ref{alg:Comb_MAB_Budget_Constrained} (\texttt{UCB-MB}) achieves expected regret $\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{A}}(B) \leq c_1 + c_2 \log(B + c_3) = O(NK^4 \log B)$.

results.notes: The paper's N (arms) is mapped to d (base arms) and its K (plays) to m. The constants hidden in the O depend on c_min, Delta_min (gap between the best and second-best K-set in bang-per-buck ratio), Delta_max and the means. The exact form c1 + c2 log(B+c3) has instance-dependent constants. Regret is the difference of expected payouts against the optimal fixed set, i.e. regret through means. The horizon is the budget-induced stopping time; the index uses log t and needs no horizon.

symbols.g: known upper bound on G_max, the maximal gain of the optimal algorithm

tuning: gamma = min(1, sqrt(N log(N/K) / (g (e-1)(1 + B/(g c_min)))))

source.label: thm:adversarial_case_bound
source.quote: Algorithm \texttt{Exp3.M.B} achieves regret \mathcal{R} \leq 2.63\sqrt{1 + \frac{B}{g c_{\min}}} \sqrt{gN\log(N/K)} + K, where $g$ is an upper bound on $G_{\max}$, the maximal gain of the optimal algorithm. This bound is of order $O(\sqrt{BN\log(N/K)})$.

results.notes: N->d, K->m. The paper also states the order O(sqrt(B N log(N/K))). The expectation is over the algorithm's internal randomness, against the best fixed K-set under the budget. 'horizon: known' refers to the known budget B.

symbols.G_max: maximal gain of the optimal fixed set of arms under budget B

conditions: Assumption 1: sum_{i in a} r_i(t) >= sum_{i in a} c_i(t) for all K-subsets a and all t
tuning: epochs r with g_r = N log(N/K)/((e-1)-(e-2)c_min) 4^r and gamma_r = min(1, 2^{-r})

source.label: prop:upper_bound_no_g
source.quote: For the multiple plays case with budget, the regret of Algorithm \texttt{Exp3.1.M.B} is upper bounded by \mathcal{R} \leq 8\left[(e-1)-(e-2)c_{\min}\right]\frac{N}{K} + 2N\log\frac{N}{K}+ K + 8 \sqrt{\left[(e-1)-(e-2)c_{\min}\right](G_{\max}-B+K)N\log(N/K)}

results.notes: N->d, K->m; E is Euler's number. Does not require knowing a bound g on G_max. The bound depends on G_max (data-dependent), so it is labelled instance_dependent.

conditions: the statement is for Algorithm Exp3.M.B
hard instance: K random good arms with Bernoulli(1/2+eps) rewards and costs in {c_min,1}

source.label: thm:lower_bound_multiple_play
source.quote: For $1\leq K \leq N$, the weak regret $\mathcal{R}$ of Algorithm \texttt{Exp3.M.B} is lower bounded as follows: \mathcal{R} \geq \varepsilon\left( B - \frac{BK}{N} - 2Bc_{\min}^{-3/2}\varepsilon\sqrt{\frac{BK\log(4/3)}{N}} \right), where $\varepsilon \in (0, 1/4]$. Choosing $\varepsilon$ as ... yields the bound \mathcal{R} \geq \min\left(\frac{c_{\min}^{3/2}(1-K/N)^2}{8\sqrt{\log(4/3)}}\sqrt{\frac{NB}{K}} ,~\frac{B(1-K/N)}{8}\right).

results.notes: N->d, K->m. The statement is restricted to Exp3.M.B, although the proof argument looks generic over algorithms, so it is recorded as algorithm_class other. Order Omega((1-K/N)^2 sqrt(NB/K)). The epsilon-parametrised intermediate bound is not recorded separately.

source.label: thm:multiple_play_fixed_round_high_probability
source.quote: For the multiple play algorithm ($1\leq K \leq N$) and a fixed number of rounds $T$, the following bound on the regret holds with probability at least $1-\delta$: \mathcal{R} = G_{\max} - G_{\texttt{Exp3.P.M}} \leq 2\sqrt{5}\sqrt{NKT\log(N/K)} + 8\frac{N-K}{N-1}\log\left( \frac{NT}{\delta} \right) + 2(1+K^2)\sqrt{NT\frac{N-K}{N-1}\log\left( \frac{NT}{\delta} \right)}.

results.notes: N->d, K->m. No costs or budget.

tuning: alpha = 2 sqrt(6) sqrt((N-K)/(N-1) log(NB/(K c_min delta)))
gamma = min((1 + 2(1-c_min)/(3 c_min))^{-1}, sqrt(3N log(N/K)/((G_max - B)(1 + 2(1-c_min)/(3c_min)))))

source.label: thm:multiple_play_budget_high_probability
source.quote: For the multiple play algorithm ($1\leq K \leq N$) and the budget $B > 0$, the following bound on the regret holds with probability at least $1-\delta$: \mathcal{R} = G_{\max} - G_{\texttt{Exp3.P.M.B}} \leq 2\sqrt{3}\sqrt{\frac{NB(1-c_{\min})}{c_{\min}}\log\frac{N}{K}} + 4\sqrt{6}\frac{N-K}{N-1}\log\left( \frac{NB}{Kc_{\min}\delta} \right) + 2\sqrt{6}(1+K^2)\sqrt{\frac{N-K}{N-1}\frac{NB}{Kc_{\min}}\log\left( \frac{NB}{Kc_{\min}\delta} \right)}

results.notes: N->d, K->m. The proof's gamma tuning involves G_max - B (and the proof uses G_max = B/c_min), so the tuning may need knowledge related to G_max. The proof has some inconsistencies.
